fact: The Gambia Press Union, in a statement to the African Commission's 87th session in Banjul, criticised the Cybercrime Bill 2023, the Communications Bill 2025 and the Criminal Offences Act 2025 as threats to media freedom.
The Gambia Press Union said criminal defamation and false publication online had previously been struck down by the Supreme Court, giving no date.

The Gambia Press Union and the Edward Francis Small Center for Rights and Justice criticised the Criminal Offence and Procedure Bill 2025, passed 24 March 2025, over its Section 49 power to ban publications and the reintroduced offence of false publication and broadcasting.

Police arrested The Voice editor Musa Sheriff and reporter Momodou Justice Darboe on 26 September 2024 over an article on the president's successor, and the High Court charged them with false publication and broadcasting on 8 October 2024, releasing them on bail.

The National Assembly passed the Criminal Offence and Procedure Bill 2025 on 24 March 2025, which replaced colonial-era laws and eliminated provisions criminalising defamation and sedition, per CIVICUS Monitor.
Freedom House says journalists in The Gambia continued to face arrests and be fined for their online commentary during the coverage period, though no prison sentences were reported.
Freedom House says an opposition member was arrested and charged with sedition in June 2024 over a WhatsApp audio message that allegedly said President Barrow knows nothing.

Freedom House says the Gambia Press Union described the false-publication and broadcasting provisions of the Criminal Offences Bill, passed by the National Assembly in March 2025, as potentially harmful to journalists and media workers.
